A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated analyses can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original hidden-state clustering, activation-steering, jailbreak and Latent Guard experiments, including additional evaluations in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical experiments and appendix evaluations, and adds numerical context for the direction-similarity analysis.

M1.justification: The difference-in-means directions, activation-addition interventions, reply-inversion procedure and Latent Guard classification rule are unchanged. Moving their descriptions does not introduce a new method.

E1.justification: Dataset and task coverage is retained, including the three jailbreak families, CATQA risk categories, ToxicChat and OpenAI Moderation evaluations. The CATQA analysis moves from v1 Section 4 to v3 Appendix D.

E2.justification: Llama Guard 3 8B remains the safeguard comparator, and the refusal-direction and category-specific comparison controls are retained. Newly cited methods are discussed rather than added to empirical comparisons.

E3.justification: The three models, sampling rules, classification threshold, inversion procedures and 50–400-example finetuning design are retained. The Llama3 Chat-to-Instruct naming correction and explicit mention of the inversion token 'No' do not establish changed experimental settings.

E4.justification: Section 3.4 adds a small reference comparison using refused and accepted instructions to contextualize whether direction similarity around 0.1 is low. Existing token-position, inversion-template, risk-category, distribution-shift and finetuning analyses remain, including those relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: Repeated-run and seed disclosures, uncertainty reporting and statistical-testing practices are unchanged. Existing plot bands are retained; the additional mean cosine similarities are results rather than new uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v3 Section 3.4 newly reports mean cosine similarities with the refusal direction of 0.57 for held-out refused instructions and -0.14 for accepted instructions. Tables 1, 3, 8 and 9 retain their values, and the matched plots retain their underlying results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–5, cluster definitions, belief scores and steering-direction definitions remain mathematically unchanged. No new theorem, proof or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract changes certain jailbreaks acting 'without reversing' harmfulness belief to acting 'without suppressing' it, slightly strengthening preservation from non-reversal to non-suppression. The central separation, categorical-representation and Latent Guard contributions otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly interprets post-instruction-token dependence as supporting template-anchored safety alignment. Section 3.4 adds reference values to justify interpreting similarity around 0.1 as low. Existing model-scale limitations, distribution-shift explanations and finetuning interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Hardware, sampling instructions, prompting templates, intervention details, finetuning description and code-access information are retained. The added Section 2 statement about 'No' restates the inversion criterion already described in v1 Section 3.5.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion and citations for ChatBug, template-anchored safety alignment, COSMIC, SafeSwitch, AdaSteer and sparse-autoencoder research. Sections 3.1 and 6 more explicitly distinguish the paper's general harmfulness representation, token-position separation and causal steering from related findings.

P1.justification: The risk-category section moves to Appendix D, and the post-finetuning refusal analysis moves to Appendix H.2. Related-work prose expands, Llama3 terminology and the publication footer are updated, and sections are renumbered; most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v1 Figure 6 becomes appendix Figure 9. v1 Figure 8 is split into v3 Figures 7 and 18, with Figure 18 receiving larger axis labels and fewer crowded layer ticks. These are presentation changes to retained results.

improvement.justification: v3 provides better research positioning, numerical context for the similarity claim and a more readable finetuning plot while retaining the original evidence and limitations. These are useful, limited quality gains. The abstract's stronger non-suppression wording lacks additional jailbreak evidence, but this small qualification does not outweigh the improvements in context and clarity.
